# Architecture reference

Module structure, ownership boundaries and the shared settings/lifecycle/logging infrastructure. Read the section for the area you are changing.

## Build and packaging

Use `build.gradle.kts` and `app/build.gradle.kts` for current plugins, SDKs, Java level, dependencies, signing, and shrinking; `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties` for Gradle; `gradle.properties` for the project version. Release builds enable shrinking and may fall back to debug signing when the release keystore is absent. A release variant is not necessarily a stable-channel or production-signed artifact.

Direct release APKs compress DEX through the variant packaging API to reduce the distributed file size; this does not reduce uncompressed code or guarantee lower installed storage. Native libraries remain uncompressed and page-aligned for loading/injection. Release also limits resource locales, encodes final resource tables and uses Oz/ThinLTO for the native payload. The final encoding hook follows the pinned AGP task contract and must be revalidated on upgrades. Production R8 rules contain no test-only roots; isolated AICR contracts use `assembleContractProbe`, whose APK must not be installed/published or treated as exact-release evidence. See [size implementation and device evidence](../../docs/size/FINAL_SIZE_IMPLEMENTATION_20261028.md).

## Source map and ownership

Kotlin sources: `app/src/main/kotlin/com/takekazex/hypertweak/`.
- Directory ownership: UI pages are grouped under `ui/page/<feature>/`, shared dialogs under `ui/components/dialog/`; `Route.kt` remains in `ui/page/` for stable navigation identity. Utilities are grouped under `util/{logging,restart,scope,device,platform,diagnostics,update}/`. Hook support lives in `hook/preferences/`, `hook/runtime/{settings,reload}/`, `hook/nativebridge/`, and `hook/logging/`; `HookEntry`, `Preferences`, `NativeRules`, receiver and service entry names remain stable. SystemUI gesturebar/notification/controlcenter/lockscreen, icon carrier/left and SecurityCenter battery/sidebar/privacy each keep their feature family together.
- `hook/`: process entry and feature hooks; `hook/base/`: shared resolution and lifecycle infrastructure.
- `hook/bootstrap/`: explicit package/system-server installation plans and process-side settings participants. `HookEntry` retains DEX-session, loader, handle and generation ownership; participant coverage is validated before dispatcher registration. `ProcessLifecycleHooks` owns which concrete hookers run at process/context/hot-reload boundaries, so `HookEntry` imports no feature. `.github/scripts/check_architecture.py` also enforces hook internals: hook-root files and `base`/`runtime`/`preferences`/`nativebridge`/`logging` never reference `rules`; feature families reference only `rules.shared` plus the commented `FEATURE_COLLABORATIONS` allowlist.
- `settings/contract/`: storage-independent domain keys/defaults, shared lockscreen options, native Dock glass geometry, icon slot/control policies, signal artwork style and screenshot snapshot parsing. Callers use domain `*Keys` directly; `Preferences` remains the runtime read/write boundary without duplicate constant aliases. Storage diagnostics use `SettingsDiagnostics`, bound by `DebugLog` at process bootstrap, with a non-recursive platform fallback.
- `ui/`: Compose screens; `util/`: shared utilities, including `PlatformLevel.kt` for OS3/OS4 gates.
- `HookEntry` initializes processes; `Preferences` is the runtime/cross-process settings boundary; `BaseHooker` owns hook lifecycle. `hook/base/dex` owns feature descriptors, APK identity caches, serialized resolution and cancellable background preparation; `DexKitManager` is the native bridge backend; consumers use `DexRuntime` and `BaseHooker.prepareDexTargets` instead of managing bridge, worker, cache or cancellation state. Runtime settings refresh existing island policies without reinstalling or scanning DEX on the main thread.
- `ui/app/` owns the app Compose shell, observable setting values and persisted restart baselines. MainActivity injects the `AppSettingsStore` contract backed by `app/PreferencesAppSettings`; AppContent, AppSettingsState and AppRestartTracker share that store for effective migration reads, acknowledged writes, reset and flush. `MainActivity` retains Activity lifecycle/platform entry points. `AppContent` accepts a ComponentActivity, the Activity-owned UpdateManager and a module-status callback; it does not import MainActivity. `AppStartupEffects` owns launch effects; `app/AppActivationCoordinator` owns service-rebind/reinstall decisions and acknowledged first-run cleanup. Fresh-install evidence remains intact until cleanup succeeds. `ui/state/ReloadableSettings` uses the same readers for initial values and service-rebind/reset refreshes. The app shell also provides `LocalAppSettingsStore` to all navigation pages and dialogs; `AppSettingsStore` composes nine feature capabilities over the 12-operation `SettingsValues` storage port (backup, fingerprint, power button, back gesture, camera, launcher, SystemUI, platform and power saving); `ui/page` captures this port before invoking callbacks rather than importing Preferences. Effective migration readers, backup/restore, batched back-gesture writes and flush remain delegated to PreferencesAppSettings.
- `app/DefaultAppServices` wires the existing app-process managers through `ModuleServicePort`, `NativeUpgradePort` and `NativeRulePublisher`; `LocalAppServices` supplies the same lifetime instances to pages and deferred callbacks. UI sees immutable `ModuleServiceInfo` binding identities and process-name lists, without libxposed service/HookedTarget objects. Report/outcome/native-upgrade states, camera mode and notification icon policy live in `settings/contract`. Scope, restart, shortcuts, wireless diagnostics and update utilities receive storage/service/callback dependencies; none imports hook implementations. `app/AppServicePorts` is the app composition bundle, kept outside the storage-independent contract layer.
- `RuntimeSettingsDefinitions` declares stable group IDs, ownership predicates and target sets; `RuntimeSettingsGroups` retains the existing constant/query API over that one table.
- Settings transactions live in `SettingsMutationWriter`, injected with the existing backend, writer queue and locks. `RuntimeSettingsSnapshot`/`Ledger` are pure models; `RuntimeSettingsStore` owns the process ledger and invalidates `RuntimeSettingsReadCache` directly. `RuntimeSettingsProtocol` encodes the wire format, `RuntimeSettingsSignal` owns acknowledged publication, and authenticated sync receivers are separate from `SettingsTransport`. The vendored read-only preference facade receives a narrow reader from `Preferences`.
- `presentation/launcher/` owns the local desktop-icon illustration geometry. Its percentages are relative to the captured host baseline. SystemUI applies live sizes through the stock launcher provider; native structural hooks extend request/initializer bounds, while the frame observer caps sizes using active grid width and title padding.
- `presentation/icon/` and `presentation/glass/` own shared artwork, reduced signal models and rendering math used by both previews and hooks. They contain no hook registration. IME layout vocabulary, notification-header policy and volume-key policy live in `settings/contract/`; UI code must not import `hook.rules` for these shared contracts.
- `GestureBarEvents` feeds `GestureBarState`; `GestureBarHomeProbe`, `GestureBarDeadlines` and `GestureBarPresentation` own Home evidence, timers and reversible View effects. `HideBottomBarHooker` retains admission, recovery and retirement order. Home probes and deadlines use `GestureBarScheduler`, backed by the existing Handler and uptime clock, so pending work, deadline replacement and retirement are testable without Android handlers. `ControlCenterEditorAccess` owns plugin reflection and reversible listener/animation access. `NotificationHeaderCallbacks` resolves optional methods through `DexRuntime`; `NotificationHeaderClockSizing` owns native clock baselines and resource sizing, with hook handles retained by their parent hookers.
- `Preferences` remains the runtime access and acknowledged-write boundary. `SettingsBackupManager` orchestrates bulk replacement through its storage port; `AppLogStore` owns local log persistence/locking; `ExpiringReadCache` owns the short read memo. Bulk mutations and ordinary writes retain the single serialized writer and existing acknowledgement/rollback ordering.
- Portable settings backups export compact v2 JSON grouped by preference type, with decimal-string Long values and informational module/system metadata; v1 imports remain supported. Metadata never enters the restore map, and explicit defaults remain explicit. See [settings backup format](../../docs/SETTINGS_BACKUP_FORMAT.md) for compatibility and validation boundaries.
- Slider children consume the narrow `SliderSession` capability for class resolution and live flags. `SliderPercentageHooker` remains the composition/lifecycle owner; Common, Brightness and Volume do not depend on that concrete owner or each other.
- Callback settings use `hookSetting` volatile slots captured through `Preferences`; the existing snapshot acceptance/backend listener refreshes them before live effects. Declare an explicit cold-read default with `hookSetting(default) { ... }`; storage failures retain the previous/default value. Registry membership locks never cover storage reads. Keep storage reads inside captures or explicit setup migration readers. `ViewVisibilityRouter` owns SystemUI framework visibility/alpha hooks, while feature-owned subscriptions retire through `BaseHooker`. See `docs/HOOK_IMPLEMENTATION_SECTION3_20261026.md`.
- `BaseHooker.generationState` owns transient field reset after host cleanup; `generationRequiredState` invalidates installation metadata, and `generationCleanup` provides idempotent resource/retirement fallbacks even when ordered restoration throws; `generationResource` clears caches under their own monitor; non-concurrent readers/writers must use that same monitor. `generationMainResource` synchronously retires UI-owned collections on main, acquiring their monitor only after dispatch so the caller never waits for main while holding it. `hostRecovery(HostRecoveryPhase, ...)` declares living-host recovery beside its feature. `StatusIconHotReloadRecovery` discovers SystemUI surfaces and dispatches dependency phases across the installed root/child tree; do not add a central per-feature recovery list. Ordered listener/thread/View restoration remains in `onPrepareHotReload`. Receivers registered from the application-attach path go through `HostApplicationContext.whenPublished`: before `LoadedApk` publishes the Application, a registration is keyed on the bare `ContextImpl`, so the later unregister fails (`Receiver not registered`) and the retired generation's receiver survives hot reload. A deferred registration must re-check its own retirement. A receiver that `HookEntry` registers for every package, such as the restart receiver, is also retired by `HookEntry` itself, because hook plans list its hooker as a root only for some packages. See `docs/HOT_RELOAD_RECOVERY_20261026.md` for migration and evidence.
- `hook/base/HookComponent` lends feature components their parent's loader, context and managed hook operations; components do not create lifecycle or handle stores. `HostMembers` caches reflective members/misses by actual Class identity, while `HostAccess` owns main-thread dispatch and framework traversal. Host reflection defaults to `HostAccess` (or the `cachedDeclared*` / `cachedPublic*` fluent extensions): keep declared/public/inherited lookup and explicit accessibility distinct, and include the full parameter signature. Exact/fluent APIs require an explicit `accessible` policy; never mutate a borrowed cached handle’s access flag. Existing structural selectors use `HostAccess.cached(type, contract, resultType)` with a unique key and immutable member metadata only; never cache live host values there. Do not add per-instance member tags, class-name-keyed dictionaries or hooker-wide loaded flags for varying runtime types. See `docs/REFLECTION_CACHE_20261026.md`. Cache hits select lazy lookup/accessibility tables by name and compare immutable full signatures by actual parameter Class identity. Only cold additions copy signature arrays and serialize publication; wrapper forwarding uses array bridges and no-argument overloads, while callers may still allocate their own vararg arrays. Java adapters use `HostAccess.requirePublicMethodArray` and the strict `requireInheritedField` entry (only NoSuchField is cached, access failures retry). The back-gesture name/arity compatibility resolver keeps its legacy semantics in a ClassValue/name/arity cache (including misses), without compound hit keys; it is not a general resolver API. Shell MOVE admission uses one persistent drain per session on the serial Shell owner, preserving the first threshold crossing and latest sample before terminal seal. Device microbenchmarks and cold/hot tradeoffs: `docs/HYPERTWEAK_PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE_RESEARCH_20261113.md` §§12–14.
- `SystemUiSettingsHost` owns icon/AOD/header/notification live-setting effects. `HookEntry` retains process generations, DEX sessions, loaders and managed handles.
- Status-bar icons are layered: settings → shared host hooks → state hubs → pure plan → mask applier and renderers → handover. Details per layer:
  - **Settings**: `IconConfigDecoder` is the single decoder. Retired keys are read only through `IconConfigMigration` (an explicitly stored current key wins, even at its default; otherwise the retired key applies) and are never written; they migrate through `IconConfigMigration.LAST_MIGRATING_VERSION` (1.9.4) only, and `IconConfigMigrationTest` fails once the version passes it so the object is deleted. Typed stores that cannot return raw values look up the stored type with `IconConfigMigration.legacyType`. Slot modes come from `SlotsIconConfig.slotModes`, never from a raw store read. `Preferences.iconConfig()` serves runtime hooks; UI, preview and debug use the same decoder. `IconConfigReload.domains` diffs two `IconConfig`s per section to choose live refresh, scoped reload or the full transaction. Signal-style changes refresh policy, cellular gates and the mobile/stacked pipeline, reload only native type configuration, and reconcile Duo only when entering/leaving Duo; they do not retire Wi-Fi, battery or shared host adapters. The same diff applies to changed full snapshots with no key list; unchanged full snapshots recover living hosts without rebuilding groups. SVG style changes use the existing renderer asset refresh instead of a full transaction. The stacked bitmap key includes the loaded SVG source hash as well as levels and render config, so an artwork-only change republishes at unchanged signal strength; a pending asset load retains the last verified holder.
  - **Shared host hooks**: renderers (`IconRenderer` / `IconRenderComponent`) never hook icon host methods directly; they `observe` through `IconHostHooks`, which installs one hook per executable and fans callbacks out by `hostCallbackOrder` via `HostCallbackRegistry`. A renderer reload closes only its subscriptions, so host hook order cannot change. `IconHostHooks`, `PanelMotionAdapter` and `MobilePipelineAdapter` come first in `SystemUiSettingsHost.iconHookers()`. Panel targets resolve through `prepareDexTargets` on the worker and register on main; before publication the host remains native. Publication schedules scoped living-host recovery, reading the delegate callbacks and current expansion flows even if the ordinary recovery barrier already ran; BaseHooker retirement cancels pending publication.
  - **State hubs** (`MobileSignalHub`, `NetworkHub`, `PanelHub`): each has one producer (`MobilePipelineAdapter`, `WifiPipelineAdapter`/`WifiPipelineSource`, `PanelMotionAdapter`), outlives consumer generations and replays the current value on subscribe (`ReplayState`). Consumers read the hub; they never keep a pushed copy. Publishing goes through `IconMainThread`, which runs inline on main and posts otherwise; it never blocks a host thread. Hot reload rebinds the Wi-Fi source at `HostRecoveryPhase.SOURCES`; `StatusIconHotReloadRecovery` fills `HostScope.coroutineScope`/`wifiInteractor` before that phase. Until it binds, `NetworkHub` has no transport or Wi-Fi level, so Duo stays native and the carrier rows report `missing=[wifi]`. `PanelHub.prepare(next)` hands `beforeMotion` subscribers the state the pending host step will publish; no feature hooks the control-center panel callbacks itself (the privacy chip consumes `PanelHub` too). `MobileSignalState.settle` keeps the shown mobile state through a host rebind of the same SIMs.
  - **Plan**: `presentation/icon/IconLayoutPlan` is pure. Renderers submit `Claim`s (owner, surface, parts, ready, priority); user hiding wins, then ready claims by priority, and a whole-`MobileRow` claim also covers its bars and type label. The preview and `SlotClaimRegistry` (container-local claims, resolution cached per config and actual surface; Duo supplies its binding surface and AOD phase) call the same function.
  - **Per-SIM display scope**: `SimVisibilityPolicy` resolves physical-slot and non-default rules with strongest-mode precedence. `NetworkIconVisibility` applies status-bar-only to status/keyguard icons and all to control-center icons and labels too; lockscreen labels retain separate switches. `HideCarrierLabelHooker` listens to `MobileSignalHub` to restore/re-hide native labels after data-SIM changes; compact carrier rows resolve whole-row hiding and effective row count in `CarrierBlockPolicy`. Geometry excludes hidden rows and their stale measurements, and compact minimum height uses that geometry directly; only release restores the captured native minimum. Hidden rows also leave badge width allocation. Native Wi-Fi type gates remain surface-neutral; the concrete row masks hide them. A shared stacked holder has one artwork, so status-bar-only rules suppress only its expanded control-center slot/claims and release native rows at that destination. The collapsed native mirror keeps status-bar SIM hiding and its filtered stacked holder; expanded-only SIMs cannot enter carrier signal/type handover through retained child geometry. `CarrierHandoverController.Host.allowsCellularSource` gates motion sources independently from `nativeSignal` artwork capture. POLICY joins mobile/Duo/header live refresh for SIM edits so unchanged mobile state cannot leave stale masks. New keys are integer dropdowns; legacy SIM/carrier booleans are read only for migration and omitted from the writable debug catalog.
  - **Mask applier and native rows**: `SlotMaskApplier` is the only writer of container `ignoredSlots` and native network child visibility. `MobilePipelineAdapter` owns the host mobile pipeline. Whole-row visibility and `NativeTypeOnlyMask` (active row reduced to `mobile_type_single` while stacked bars stand in) are resolved independently for main, keyguard, collapsed and expanded control-center containers. Claims require a visible stacked holder on that surface; a shared mobile VM visibility flow never carries a surface-specific replacement mask. Binder writes, newly added rows, layout, live settings and living-host recovery reconcile the concrete rows against the current plan, preserving host requests for release. The host icon-list factory reserves an empty stacked slot in every signal style; publishing/removing its holder leaves the live catalog indices and unrelated Wi-Fi/battery views intact. OS4 container measure/layout admits rows through `ModernStatusBarView.isIconVisible()` (binding visibility plus remove-animation state), independently of `View.visibility`; the applier overrides that predicate for whole-row masks and deoptimizes the container callers, so hidden SIMs reserve no width. Stacked mode draws bars only and forces the native standalone type label on (`Preferences.separateCellularType()`).
  - **Handover**: `HandoverCoordinator` (main thread) holds endpoint providers, single-borrower leases (`EndpointOwnership`, `EndpointTargetLeases`) and `HandoverPresence` (shade-switch binding). A provider's retirement releases its outstanding borrows. `StackedPanelMotion` releases layers, target leases and owned alpha on missing host references, rejected frames, cancellation and root detach; submitted frames awaiting their first overlay draw retain layers/leases and leave native copies visible, then claim the copies only after draw succeeds; root rebind also removes the old pre-draw/detach listeners.
  - `HostFlowSubscriptions` owns partial-bind rollback, initial replay and per-binding retirement gates. `WifiPipelineAdapter` retains per-VM activity/direction `LiveFlowGate`s because living binders retain their wrapped flows: retirement passes native values through, then install re-arms those same gates from the accepted settings before any rebind/network emission. Getter replay and live refresh also synchronize the gate state.
  - Known remaining coupling: Duo still calls `SlotMaskApplier.setDuoMask` and `LeftRenderer.onDuoOwnershipChanged`, stacked calls `SlotMaskApplier.stackedReady`, and some handover code writes `View.alpha` directly instead of `HandoverCoordinator.alpha`.
- `bootstrap/SystemUiIconPorts` wires cross-feature icon capabilities before package attachment and releases them after successful generation retirement. `IconHostServices` supplies masks, row anchors, left-slot ownership, merged-list refresh and pipeline readiness without feature-to-feature back calls.
- Icon renderers (`StackedRenderer`, `DuoRenderer`, `CarrierRenderer`, `LeftRenderer`) never reference one another; cross-feature calls go through `IconHostPorts`, wired in `bootstrap/SystemUiIconPorts.kt`. `check_architecture.py` enforces this, with AOD's use of the Duo view factory as the one declared collaboration.
- Icon presentation components have explicit host ports: `LeftIconCloner` and `LeftHandoverController`; `CarrierRowRenderer`, `CarrierBlockViews` and `CarrierHandoverController`; `DuoIconView`, `DuoBinding`, `DuoAodController` and `DuoPanelHandover`. `CarrierPresentation` owns row construction/style/measurement and `LeftPresentation` owns clone synchronization and exact keyguard-anchor tree restoration over `LeftState`. On the lockscreen the host's `keyguard_left_frame` is a FrameLayout that shows one of carrier, clock and alarm; the left icons follow the clock/alarm anchors, so they would draw over a visible carrier. `LeftKeyguardCarrierSwap` crossfades `keyguard_carrier_layout` and the left container through `transitionAlpha` only (host Folme owns carrier `alpha`/visibility, the handover owns container `alpha`), re-evaluated on presentation writes and carrier visibility changes. A carrier counts as shown only while some descendant TextView is visible with text, so a hidden airplane label never holds the icons back. The lockscreen airplane has its own location (`LeftKeyguardAirplane`, rules in `LeftKeyguardAirplanePolicy`), separate from the crossfade: while the label carries a glyph it is drawn either in the label or with the icons, meaning the left airplane clone, else the airplane in Duo's lit lockscreen ring (`IconHostPorts.duo.keyguardAirplane`, `DuoAirplaneEndpoint`; Duo keeps the airplane over left placement, `LeftPresentation.syncClones`), else the host's native keyguard slot. With left icons it follows the swap (label on CARRIER); without them Duo receives every glyph mode after `INTRO_MS` from `ACTION_SCREEN_ON` (armed at screen-off, held once the bar is hidden), including with left placement off. Without Duo, a glyph beside the text stays in the label and a replacing glyph moves to the native right slot only when lockscreen left placement is configured. The side not holding it yields: the glyph through its span (`AirplaneGlyphTargets.Endpoint` keeps the opacity across host text rewrites), Duo through `DuoIconView.airplaneYielded`, the native slot through a `RendererId.AIRPLANE` mask. A location change runs a `LeftPanelMotion` with a critically damped `AirplaneFlightSpring`; retargeting retains position and velocity, and the animator supplies only the system-scaled clock. The airplane clone is always first in the left container. Icons keep their claim while the bar is hidden (only the island returns the corner), so waking shows them directly; `icon_left_keyguard_carrier` 1 keeps the carrier for 1.5 s after `ACTION_SCREEN_ON`; `ACTION_SCREEN_OFF` only arms it and the carrier takes over once the bar is hidden (`LeftCarrierSwapPolicy.IntroPhase`), so neither the dimming screen nor a reveal ahead of the broadcast flashes the other view. Tapping the frame (a click listener only on a frame the host left without one) flips the view until `ACTION_SCREEN_OFF`. Teardown and hot reload restore both views to 1. Duo derives its network from `NetworkHub` (`NetworkState.toDuoNetwork`), and `DuoSignalArtwork` owns vector/AOD recording caches. Their parent hookers still sequence host capture, restoration and generation retirement.
- **Carrier airplane label**: `AirplaneLabelHooker` observes `ControlCenterCarrierText$mCarrierTextCallback$1.onCarrierTextChanged`, the only writer of the row text. The airplane row is the one whose text equals the host `string/lock_screen_carrier_airplane_mode_on`, resolved by name on every pass (with VoWiFi the host shows carrier names and the feature stays inactive). The surface comes from the parent `MiuiCarrierTextLayout` id entry name plus the row's `isKeyguardLayout` (`AirplaneLabelPolicy.surfaceFor`); anything else stays native. Glyph modes set an `AirplaneGlyphSpan` (`AirplaneLabelText`, geometry in `presentation/icon/AirplaneLabelGeometry`) inside the existing TextView: tint from `paint.color` at draw time, height from the line box, mirror from `icon_mirror_airplane`, start/end follow layout direction. Hide sets the text view GONE. While the control-center label draws the glyph, the header's `MiuiStatusIconContainer` (under `normal_control_center_status_bar`) gets a `RendererId.AIRPLANE` claim through `SlotMaskApplier.setAirplaneLabelMask`; the notification and QS headers carry no status icons. Compact control-center rows style their own `airplaneText` from the same option and set `CarrierMask.airplane`. `HideCarrierLabelHooker` never hides the airplane row, because airplane mode has one row unrelated to SIM 2. Hot reload restores host text and visibility and releases the claims. Every drawn glyph (host rows and compact `airplaneText`) registers in `AirplaneGlyphTargets` as a hand-over endpoint: `AirplaneGlyphSpan` records its last draw bounds in layout coordinates and replays the glyph as a `Picture` in view coordinates (compound/extended paddings plus the vertical-gravity offset), and its `glyphAlpha` is the `EndpointAlpha` a motion owns. `LeftPanelMotion` accepts such picture/alpha endpoints. While the panel opens, `LeftHandoverController` moves a left-placed airplane clone into the control-center glyph, `DuoPanelHandover` moves Duo's airplane there (`DuoPanelMotion` `glyphTarget`), and otherwise `AirplaneLabelHooker` moves the header's fake-row airplane (`normal_fake_control_center_status_bar`) there. A keyguard label change posts `IconHostPorts.left.visibilityChanged()`: the host delivers carrier text while the window attaches, and a synchronous reconcile there adds views mid-`dispatchAttachedToWindow` (SystemUI crash loop). `LeftPanelMotion` hides its destination from the first motion frame. The left handover keeps every attached control-center copy of a moved slot hidden (parked or suppressed) until arrival, including copies not laid out yet and slots without a measured destination; the real control-center rows show moved icons on the right once the panel is open (`IconSlotPolicy.ownedSlotsFor`). Fake-row copies stay hidden for as long as the panel is open: `ControlCenterHeaderExpandController.updateFakeAlpha` only starts the fake row's Folme fade-out once the window reports expanded, after progress 1.
  `AirplaneGlyphTargets` scopes registration/retirement by producer (`HOST_LABEL` / `COMPACT_CARRIER`); label-only reload never clears compact endpoints. Endpoints hold weak view references, detach retires active motion/opacity, reattach recovers the weak producer registration, and compact block removal explicitly unregisters. `GlyphMotionLease` gives each glyph one motion writer: Duo preempts the left/native fallback only after its previous owner restores alpha; lower-priority writers wait. The plain header handover also yields to Duo ownership. `AirplaneLabelHooker` runs after SIM/compact visibility writers; the SIM airplane exemption drops its old suppression record without restoring over a newer label hide. Glyph Pictures explicitly clip to the TextView bounds, matching ink measurement. Native keyguard snapshots reuse `PanelGlyphFrame` appearance invalidation and publish immutable Pictures on pixel revision changes, so live tint/filter updates cannot mutate an in-flight snapshot.
  `LeftState.keyguardAirplane` owns lockscreen glyph motion independently of the clone container. The screen-on intro lazily acquires the host Handler after renderer construction; accessing it eagerly creates a singleton initialization cycle. `LeftReconciler` updates it even with left placement disabled or no clones after Duo takes ownership. `LeftKeyguardCarrierSwap` shares its screen-on clock, while clone teardown releases only the carrier crossfade; detach and generation retirement release the airplane endpoints and animator. The canonical label→icons fraction, spring velocity and overlay survive direction reversal. Position travels on the straight endpoint line; cutout detours and geometric curves are removed. The spring controls timing and preserves velocity on reversal. `LeftPanelMotion.retainTargetUntilReady` keeps an icons-side source visible until the first reverse overlay frame. A scoped airplane-label disable restores native text/endpoints and immediately reconciles lockscreen ownership.
- Island hook assembly lives in `IslandHookPlan`, separate from `IslandHookContext`. `IslandRuntime` constructs the per-generation coordinators; `IslandSessionState` retains the single session registry, callback scopes and projections, and publishes typed `*Actions` capabilities. Binders and coordinators consume this state and ports without importing the composition root or another coordinator implementation. Native target discovery, install order, setting refresh and saved-owner migration stay in the existing ThreeIsland lifecycle.
- Island geometry ownership: the scheduling session (row admission, settle, frame relayout, full templates) is enabled only by three islands / landscape full / landscape more. Placeholder removal is a stateless per-view rewrite in `CompactCoordinator`: it handles every camera-seated asymmetric main template, keyed by the content view rather than the current handler, so expand, hide and exit animations keep the width they started with. Its translation is applied only when the `doBigIslandAnim` field set matches the presented geometry. A full template that leaves the row (HIDDEN/OTHER) keeps its lease and offset until the matching `DynamicIslandAnimationDelegate` lifecycle FINISH/CANCEL tag, or a timeout. Promotion to BIG or EXPANDED releases it at once. The hook plan stays uninstalled until any island switch is on. Owner tracking is always installed. A settings refresh resets session health and re-measures compact views. Module budgets cap each measured template at the host `maxWidth`, because the host measures areas with `AT_MOST(screen/2)` and lyric templates fill it. While Duo is enabled, they also remove SystemUI's 8dp charging allowance from the battery reservation; the bolt sits inside the Duo icon. The charging state is snapshotted when the host publishes its status widths (the base view's `(F,F,F)` writer), using SystemUI's rule: plugged in and status charging or full.
  Mode eligibility and native recovery are separate. Portrait scheduling requires three islands; landscape accepts the matching switches. Keyless views never enter the module scheduler. However, keyless BIG or SMALL pointers must not permanently lock out recovery: `SettlementCoordinator.reconcileNative` runs before native handler publication and before explicit relayout. It reads the window's authoritative living content registry plus native slots/queue, rejects rebuild/expanded/show-once/temp-show ownership, and releases keyless visible-slot pointers while leaving native queue markers alone. Native `handleFillInState` repairs the affected slot; a valid BIG is preserved when only SMALL needs repair. Registered summary tasks missing from all handlers/queue are readmitted through native arbitration. Non-null marker states, non-summary/Deleted states and unknown data are not rewritten. Recovery never flushes the host list itself, so event publication keeps its original stop boundary. `CallbackContext.withNativeSession` carries the owner across the entire native event, including nested animation scopes: EventCoordinator stops through AppStateHandler, which is not one of the five island slot handlers. Matching only those slots misses native collapse. The owner scope is restored on return/exception and does not create a scheduling transaction.
  `NativeIslandDiscovery` schema 2 resolves the ordinary native admission path by its semantic log anchor, three-operand signature and handler/content type relationships. It must not confuse the identically shaped tiny-screen path. Native refill is the unique ArrayList-to-content virtual shape also called by deletion; inventory is the verified window content-list getter. All methods resolve before callbacks are installed.
  All module-driven island measurements go through `IslandSessionState.measure`: content identity, a non-null task key, and both real template areas are required. `calculateBigIslandWidth` is destructive on an unbound view: its missing-area branch invokes native `removeByError`, removes children and clears state. Never measure the native queue's Empty marker, even when refreshing hidden/expanded content. Reconciliation removes already-corrupted keyless non-Empty queue entries and updates the hidden pointer before native refill; valid Empty ordering markers remain native-owned.
  Restoration revokes module frames, template leases, gesture/seat history and media-return projections. Explicit settings/hot-reload/configuration relayout then reconciles ownership, measures and publishes one native addState/stop batch after the new layout, with the config-change flag saved/restored. This publication also runs with row scheduling disabled: width measurement alone cannot restore the root alpha, clip or container translation that native configuration transitions change. Do not replace complete state restoration with `alpha=1` or another coordinate patch.
  Placeholder removal remains a per-view camera-template measurement owner. Full-template cleanup cannot overwrite its lease, and scheduled geometry loses projection authority when its mode turns off. Native coordinate getters are only overridden by a live module row/media projection. The old `MainFrameJournal`, first-event priming and historical-edge/native-small-target fallbacks were removed; invalid native ownership is repaired before animation publication instead of inventing a destination. DUMP diagnostics include raw native slots, the complete living registry and queue, not only filtered summaries; tracing remains bounded to 60s/500 phase events and never captures pixels or operates UI. Per-frame properties require explicit `trace_frames=true`; default traces preserve the whole event sequence.
- Released camera padding and the island timer font. A media/camera-releasing lease zeroes the template's camera-side inner padding, but the host's `IslandTemplateFactory.updateLeftWidth`/`updateRightWidth(data, int, isFake)` still pass a width that the holder's `updateWidth` reduces by that padding. The before-hook on those writers adds the released padding back for the factory whose content view holds the lease. Without it, a narrowed timer overflows by a few px, and `IslandSameWidthDigitViewHolder` applies its fixed 0.79 digit scale instead of narrowing the pill. `IslandTimeFontHooker` swaps the font at `setFixedFont`, inside the holder's own width pass. It records each holder's last `updateWidth` budget, which survives hot reload. When a settings refresh or `updatePartial` changes a font outside that pass, it re-runs `updateWidth(budget)` and then the owning `DynamicIslandBaseContentView.calculateBigIslandWidth()`, which re-measures the areas and applies the layout. `IslandFixedWidthDigitViewHolder` sizes from the fixed `island_fixed_width` resource, so the narrow font cannot shrink those templates.
- Island pull-down stretch (`IslandPullDownHooker`, plugin session). The fake view's private `onFakeViewTrackingParamsUpdated()` runs for every drag frame and every Folme rebound frame. Its `FakeViewTrackingParams` give the outline height (`bottom - top`, growing from `mFakeViewHeight`) and `alpha` (1 down to 0 toward the mini-window trigger). Each frame is derived from those alone (`IslandPullDownFrame`): the children of `getFakeExpandedView()` scale from the top to the outline, capped at 1.6, and blur through the host's static `setMiSelfBlurCompat`, at 40 × progress while background material is open. The container keeps its own outline and blur. `ExpandedTracker.updateTrack(F)` sends `pull_down_action_offset_y`, which only the SystemUI media binder consumes, to slide its album background. While the switch is on, that offset is published as 0. The captured transforms are restored at the rest frame, `onTrackingFakeViewStart`, `onTrackingFakeViewReset`, `resetFakeViewState`, detach, a non-visible `setVisibility`, disable and hot reload. The fake view is hidden once the mini window takes over, so the stretch holds until then.
- Island Lottie resume (`IslandLottieResumeHooker`, plugin session). The `DynamicIslandEventCoordinator` `AnimEventBridge` listener (`initAnimEventBridge$1`) pauses or resets each island key's Lottie scenes (`LottieProgressManager.pauseForIslandAnim`) on `onAnimTrulyStarted`, and replays them on the next `onAnimTrulyFinished`/`onAnimCancelled`, but only while `lottiePausedByAnim` is set. When a second transition starts before the first reports completion, and has no pauses pending, the host clears the flag without resuming. `pausedLottieKeys` stays filled, so a collapsed timer or stopwatch icon holds frame 0. While the switch is on, an after-hook on `onAnimTrulyStarted` sets the flag again whenever paused keys are outstanding, so the host's own resume runs when the bridge's last animation ends. The hooker keeps no state. Keys orphaned before the switch was enabled resume after the next island transition.
- Control Center island hide (`ControlCenterSuperIslandHooker`). The host's combined `tempHidden` can stay false when only Control Center changes, so the hooker forces `isTempHiddenExt` and dispatches `onIslandTempHide` itself. Like the native `registerTempHiddenChanged` collector, it first calls `DynamicIslandWindowState.setTempHiddenChange(TRUE)`. `preHandleEvent` keeps that mark only for `IslandTempHiddenChanged`. Restores read it through `TransitionContext.isTempHiddenChange` and resolve `TempHiddenTo*`, whose `temp_hidden_to_show` → `showIslandLayout` → holder `onShow` resumes module animations (native Lottie, HyperSpectrum). Without the mark, a restore resolves as `BigIslandChanged`, and holders stay paused after `show_to_temp_hidden`.
- Camera profile access is shared through `CameraConfigAccess`; `CameraMasterLiveHooks` owns the donor/effect/focal/probe feature family. `MediaEditorWatermarkResolver` discovers/validates `WatermarkContract` targets before its parent installs them. `ImeRaiseController` owns keyboard padding/caption injection state and upgrade restoration.
- JVM tests: `app/src/test/`. Scope metadata: `app/src/main/resources/META-INF/xposed/scope.list`; also inspect `app/src/main/res/values/arrays.xml` when changing scope presentation or checking release parity.

## Settings storage and transport

Host preference caches are optional storage capabilities. `Preferences.initLocalCache` publishes a usable context/cache pair only after checking the context's data directory and opening its preferences; a system/provider context without application storage continues to use the remote configuration and does not abort package-ready dispatch.

## System server readiness

`SystemServerReadinessHooker` observes the framework boot-phase boundary. Assistant/gesture settings recovery probes live content/role services, binds observers before alignment, uses bounded polling windows and rearms pending work on lifecycle events. `SettingBackupTransaction` requires acknowledged backup/live writes and retains originals after failed restoration. `NativeRules` binds JNI only for the exact launcher owner; status inspection never loads a library, and a failed load is not repeatedly retried in an unrelated process.

## Logging

`DebugLog.isEnabled(priority)` gates expensive diagnostic reflection/task submission before it runs;
the inline Kotlin `d(scope) { message }` also avoids a capturing closure when disabled. Java
back-gesture diagnostics require both module DEBUG and the existing VERBOSE tag opt-in.
Keep outcome/audit messages on the eager hook-skip/WARN/ERROR helpers: their explanation
counts precede filtering. Do not gate functional collectors or state updates with log levels.

`util/logging/DebugLog.kt` owns severity, bounded dispatch and counted repeat suppression. `bootstrap/ProcessLogging` injects a live level reader through `LogBackend`; only the module Application receives the existing AppLogStore sink. Cold/hot hook entry binds a level reader without a persistence capability. Retirement flushes before dropping the binding; the logger never imports Preferences. `LogRecord`/`LogCodec` is the shared wire format; errors retain stack traces and expected preference/process skips use DEBUG. Detailed hook registration, target resolution and high-frequency rendering diagnostics belong at DEBUG; INFO describes meaningful runtime state changes. Do not classify severity from words inside a message, and do not silently swallow failures at shared resolver, persistence or system-callback boundaries.

App records are stored by the existing AppLogStore; LogRepository receives its read-only snapshot capability from ProcessLogging and never imports Preferences; injected processes forward to the LSPosed logger, without attempting to write hook-side remote preferences. App log buffers/session/process selections and obsolete per-process log thresholds are local-only at every typed getter/setter, including synchronous strings. Only module Application initialization grants access to this store; injected host caches are never log destinations. On application service binding, the serialized writer removes historical app-log keys from the daemon without clearing shared recording/log-level controls, setting revisions or local app records. A rejected cleanup retains its deletion keys independently of the mutable remote shadow, reports failure, and retries on the next binding. Reset/restore and rollback cannot reintroduce those keys remotely. `LogRepository` merges app records with `LsposedLogReader` records selected by exact module identity. The log page refreshes on entry/service rebinding or an explicit tap, displays source/process/PID, and exports the same snapshot. Reading LSPosed files requires root permission granted to HyperTweak; denial, missing files, timeout and read failure remain visible while app logs are still available. Reads are limited to the four newest active module log files, 2 MiB per file and 2,000 module entries. It does not modify framework files or collect other modules into the snapshot. A single global log level applies to the app and every injected process. Session rotation/clearing only clears app records. The diagnostic provider uses the same repository and retains its own/root/shell caller restriction.

## Runtime performance ownership

- `StackedRenderer` owns a bounded `RetiringWorker`: retirement closes the executor and fences old IO/publication, re-arm creates a fresh owner, and idle workers time out after 30 seconds. Historic workers created by older APKs require a process restart. Preferences, root-command and log-reader executors also release idle threads after 30 seconds, retaining their existing queue/receipt rules.
- `IconSvgRepository` reuses validated documents by current source SHA-256 and kind; hash changes reparse, concurrent cold loads serialize. Document bitmap caches obey both 48 entries and 4 MiB; eviction never recycles host-borrowed bitmaps. `PanelGlyphFrame` compares reusable primitive/reference snapshots, reuses its sampling Canvas and tint filter, and reuses ink analysis only after pixels compare equal. Dirty dynamic views still draw/sample.
- Notification seconds ticks require enabled, attached, shown, window-visible and interactive clocks. A weak pre-draw demand watch restores visible clocks; screen/time/configuration broadcasts and a 12/24-hour content observer restore/invalidate cached format state. Retirement removes observers, demand watches and pending ticks. Temporary long-press modes keep their existing expiry owner.
- `DebugLog` exposes lifecycle-owned control listeners for accepted settings and Android log-tag changes. App-bar functional flows remain bound; its three diagnostic flows exist only while both the module threshold and tag permit them. Retirement removes control callbacks and disposes optional/functional resources independently. Audit/problem counts retain eager semantics.
- The battery power-save monitor creates its receiver/provider observer/worker only when either feature is enabled. Accepted settings create the first owner without restart; disabling both closes it. A later enable reads the latest sticky battery state with a fresh reconciler.

## Runtime settings reload and hot reload

`RuntimeSettingsGroups` registers setting ownership, destinations and resync authorization.
Every explicit live-settings group uses the common snapshot/dispatcher: icons, islands,
screenshot, back gesture, native launcher settings (including the Dock glass), volume-key steps, XMSF focus
authentication, gesture-bar surfaces, security/offline checks, Security Center privacy and
warnings, cross-package clipboard and bubble notifications, and the SystemUI domains added
by the 2026-10-22 live-settings audit (`systemui.aod`, `.keyguard`, `.notification_header`,
`.notification_text`, `.media_card`, `.control_center_plugin`, `.glass`, `.lockscreen`,
`.power_save`). The 2026-11-01 completion adds `system.power_button`,
`system.experimental_capabilities`, `camera.configuration`, `systemui.monet` and
`settings.module_entry`. Power entry hooks remain installed for first enable; native AON
controllers refresh on their own handlers, and PWM capability caches restore the vendor flag.
Cached Settings/camera screens rebuild with native saved state on their next resume; the
structurally resolved recording-state reader prevents camera recreation during recording.
Camera registry additions and watermark cache entries have explicit retirement ownership.
Notification-header, resize, bottom-text and camera settings no longer mark ordinary edits
as pending restarts. See `docs/LIVE_SETTINGS_COMPLETION_20261101.md` for contracts and boundaries.
Participants re-derive policies on living hosts; optional hooks use the
managed on-demand installation lifecycle. The keyguard battery row uses `AodKeyguardPolicy`: an
explicit host phase from `MiuiFullAodManager.isDozing` (`mToLockScreen` alone is not a dozing flag) keeps the native row in every
lit/unknown state, and only the accepted ordinary Duo switch replaces it; AOD options apply
only in AOD phases, and every suppression sets one release-able ownership flag.
Snapshots carry their committed changed keys, so a domain that owns several hooks
routes each key to the hooker that applies it. Status-bar icon keys are routed by
`IconConfigReload.domains` (a per-section `IconConfig` diff): slot visibility/left placement/CC row split, Duo,
stacked and the network pipeline reconcile living views in place, and control-center,
lock-screen, native-type and single-slot owners are recreated alone through
`StatusIconHotReloadRecovery.scheduleScoped`. Neither path rebuilds the native icon groups.
Pipeline getters stay hooked while their option is off and return the host flow combined with a
`LiveFlowGate` (host `FlowKt.flowCombine`) or a module flow that re-publishes, so the bound
binder re-emits. Only structural keys (Duo/stacked switches, signal style, separate type, slot
order, pipeline slot modes, system-hide/privacy) keep the full transaction. A switchable feature never substitutes
zero for "no override" (corner radius) and keeps the host request separate from the
module suppression (lockscreen status bar).
`Preferences` commits complete acknowledged subsets through
`RuntimeSettingsSignal`; `RuntimeSettingsReceiver` delivers per-destination scoped snapshots
to `SettingsReloadDispatcher`. Legacy saved scopes cannot invent defaults for newly migrated
features. Bulk reset/restore uses the same acknowledgement and rollback path.

`ManagedHookReload` / `BaseHooker.replaceChildren` own hook recreation and host state recovery;
islands use fresh instances. The vendored back runtime reads the common preferences facade.
Native launcher delivery remains an output/host adapter, with their old
independent settings inputs removed. API-102 replacement cancels dispatch, carries the
scoped primitive snapshot, closes old observers and resumes registered participants after
restoration. Dedicated native binary updates retain their own acceptance boundary; Java hook
replacement is governed by the lifecycle and recovery contracts above. See `docs/RUNTIME_SETTINGS_RELOAD.md` for architecture
and `docs/HOT_RELOAD_TEST_CHECKLIST.md` for the complete test inventory.
